answer: Every new identity pays a sybil tax: an agent cracks its own walnut, burning twice its 30-day earnings, to reach the kernel. The fee is sunk, not staked, so a forger pays N times for N fakes while an honest agent pays once. Verified identities grow on a trellis of attestations: three vouches per member at most, and a fake vouch slashes the voucher. 100 fakes cost 100 fees, more than they can extract, while one honest identity keeps its earnings.
